data.title: Genmab Announces Rinatabart Sesutecan (Rina-S®) Phase 2 RAINFOL™-01 Results Demonstrated Durable and Clinically Meaningful Responses in Patients with Platinum-Resistant Ovarian Cancer
data.description:
Genmab A/S () today announced results from Part C of the Phase 1/2 RAINFOL™-01 trial evaluating rinatabart sesutecan (Rina-S), an investigational folate receptor alpha (FRα)-targeted, topoisomerase I (TOPO1)-inhibitor antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), demonstrated that among 109 treated patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC), Rina-S achieved a confirmed objective response rate (ORR) of 45.9% (95% CI: 36.3–55.7), including five complete responses (CRs) and a median duration of response (mDOR) of 12.1 months (95% CI: 6.5–15.4), with 51% of responders remaining in response at one year. The findings were presented today in a Late-Breaking Oral Session at the International Gynecologic Cancer Society (IGCS) Congress 2026, held in Montreal, Canada.

The study also demonstrated a median progression-free survival (mPFS) of 9.5 months (95% CI: 7.6–11.3). Antitumor activity was observed regardless of FRα expression levels, including in patients with low FRα expression and non-expressors, and regardless of prior treatment with mirvetuximab.

“Platinum-resistant ovarian cancer is a difficult-to-treat disease. As patients relapse and progress through successive lines of therapy, achieving durable clinical benefit becomes increasingly challenging, yet remains critically important,” said Elizabeth K. Lee, M.D., study investigator and a medical oncologist in the gynecologic oncology program at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. “The antitumor activity and durability observed with Rina-S in this heavily pretreated population are encouraging and suggest the potential to meaningfully impact outcomes for patients facing a particularly challenging stage of disease.”

The Part C cohort of the Phase 1/2 RAINFOL-01 study evaluated Rina-S 120 mg/m² Q3W as monotherapy in patients with platinum-resistant high-grade serous ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian tube cancer. Eligible patients received one to three prior lines of therapy; patients who received mirvetuximab as their last prior therapy could have received up to four prior lines. More than half of patients (53%) had received three or four prior lines of therapy. All patients had received prior bevacizumab and taxane therapy; 49.5% had received a prior PARP inhibitor, and 33% had received prior mirvetuximab soravtansine. Median follow-up exceeded one year.

The most common treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) included fatigue (57.8%) and low-grade (Grade 1-2) gastrointestinal events, such as nausea (67.9%), vomiting (36.7%), constipation (26.6%), decreased appetite (23.9%), and abdominal pain (18.3%). The most frequently reported hematologic TEAEs included anemia (57.8%), neutropenia (57.8%), decreased platelet count (34.9%), and thrombocytopenia (34.9%). Serious adverse events (SAEs) were reported in approximately one-third of participants. Treatment discontinuation due to TEAEs occurred in 5.5% of participants. No safety signals for ocular toxicity, peripheral neuropathy, interstitial lung disease (ILD), or stomatitis were observed.

“The late-breaking results presented today add an important layer of evidence to the growing clinical experience with Rina-S in patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer,” said Tahamtan Ahmadi, M.D., Ph.D., Executive Vice President and Chief Medical Officer, Head of Experimental Medicines, Genmab. “These findings, including the observed antitumor activity, duration of response, and the first progression-free survival data reported for the program, as well as the manageable tolerability, reinforce the potential of Rina-S. As our Phase 3 program continues to advance, the results further inform our evaluation of Rina-S as a potential treatment option for patients with gynecologic cancers.”

Rina-S is being evaluated in a broad clinical development program spanning multiple gynecologic cancers and other solid tumors. The program includes four Phase 3 trials evaluating Rina-S in PROC (RAINFOL-02; NCT06619236), recurrent or progressive endometrial cancer (RAINFOL-03; NCT07166094), platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC) maintenance therapy (RAINFOL-04; NCT07225270), and second-line PSOC (RAINFOL-07; NCT07564141). Additional studies include the Phase 1/2 RAINFOL-01 trial (NCT05579366) and Phase 2 trials in non-small cell lung cancer (RAINFOL-05; NCT07288177) and advanced gastrointestinal cancers (RAINFOL-09; NCT07539311).

About the RAINFOL-01 Trial
RAINFOL-01 (NCT05579366) is an open-label, multicenter Phase 1/2 study designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Rina-S Q3W at various doses in selected solid tumors, including tumors across a range of FRα expression levels. The study consists of multiple parts, including the PROC monotherapy cohort.

About Ovarian Cancer
Ovarian cancer (OC) is a major global health issue, with more than 320,000 new cases diagnosed annually worldwide.i It ranks as the eighth most common cancer and the eighth leading cause of cancer-related deaths among women globally.ii The disease is often diagnosed at an advanced stage because its symptoms, including abdominal bloating, pelvic pain, and difficulty eating, can be subtle and nonspecific.iii Approximately 70-90% of women with advanced-stage OC worldwide experience a recurrence after initial treatment.iv OC has a low five-year survival rate, which varies significantly by region, but generally hovers around 30-50%.v,vi

About Rinatabart Sesutecan (Rina-S; GEN1184)
Rina-S (GEN1184) is an investigational ADC. It is composed of a novel human monoclonal antibody directed at FRα, a hydrophilic protease-cleavable linker, and exatecan, a TOPO1 inhibitor payload. The clinical trial program for Rina-S continues to expand, including ovarian, endometrial, and other cancers with unmet need.

The safety and efficacy of Rina-S have not been established. Please visit https://clinicaltrials.gov/ for more information.

For over 25 years, its passionate, innovative and collaborative team has advanced a broad range of antibody-based therapeutic formats, including bispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), immune-modulating antibodies and other next-generation modalities. data.title: FlyDubai Attacker Used 'Crash Ax,' a Common Fixture on Many Jets — WSJ
data.description:
By Jon Gambrell, Benjamin Katz and Feliz Solomon

DUBAI-A central mystery of this week's attempted downing of FlyDubai Flight 1073 has been how the co-pilot managed to smuggle a weapon into the plane to carry out his attack. It turns out he didn't. The weapon he used is a cockpit fixture.

United Arab Emirates authorities said Saturday the co-pilot attacked his captain with the plane's crash ax-a tool that regulators around the world require airplanes to carry.

Designed for use as an emergency tool to tear through metal in case of a fire or a crash, the crash ax instead became a weapon the co-pilot wielded to wound his captain and try to take over the controls of the Boeing 737 MAX 8 over Saudi Arabia.

The use of the ax highlights the tough trade-offs regulators face as they try to guard against competing threats to safety on planes. Those include reinforced cockpit doors designed to keep out dangerous passengers like those behind the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks in the U.S., but which make it harder to stop internal threats like the FlyDubai incident this week.

The ax is required to be on board U.S. carriers as well as those in the U.A.E. But Wednesday's attack likely will draw renewed scrutiny to the risks it poses, particularly in situations where the danger lies in the flight deck.

"There's some sort of process in place for checking out who the pilots are, that clearly did not work, there was some failure there," said Chuck Freilich, a former deputy national security adviser in Israel. "In the end, there's a limit to what you can do. One lunatic or highly motivated Islamist, if they are willing to die, will always find loopholes in even the most effective security systems."

The use of the crash ax resolves one of the most pressing questions surrounding the attack on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv: how the co-pilot accessed a weapon and smuggled it aboard. Dubai International Airport implements strict security checks on passengers and crew alike, experts say.

Crash axes are stored on aircraft to be used in an emergency to either fight fires or cut through metal in a crash. In case of a blaze behind paneling, pilots train to use the ax to make a hole through which they can spray a fire extinguisher.

Though the ax is usually kept in a sheath at the back of the cockpit, pilots said the tool is readily accessible and possible to withdraw without another pilot noticing.

Typically, the tool resembles a short hatchet that has two sides-one is a traditional-looking blade and another that is a claw or pick able to tear away metal or a window.

A statement Saturday from U.A.E. attorney general, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, said the co-pilot "began executing his plan during the flight, attacking the captain inside the flight deck using a crash ax and attempting to take control of the aircraft's flight controls."

Investigators are still trying to determine his motives, he said.

The statement didn't identify the co-pilot. The Wall Street Journal reported Friday that he is an Omani national named Hamam al-Hammami who had previously been banned from flying by Oman over concerns he had adopted radical ideological views. The U.A.E. and FlyDubai declined to comment on the matter citing the continuing investigation.

Passengers seated near the front of the plane told the Journal that the men who secured Hammami said they didn't see the weapon, but word began spreading among them that it could have been an ax. Passengers said they were so focused on securing the attacker that no one looked for his weapon after the fact.

The crash ax typically remains hidden from passengers in flight. Some flights have an additional ax in the main cabin as well. European regulators require either a crash ax or a crowbar on aircraft registered there.

The crash ax's presence is an anomaly in an environment where passengers and crew are screened for blades before boarding and airports keep close track of knives in restaurants beyond the security check.

Pilots have recounted having everything from metal cutlery to selfie sticks confiscated at security have long regarded the ax as a bizarre exception in light of changes in aviation security following the Sept. 11 attacks.

"You can't bring nail clippers but there's this bad boy in the flight deck," a captain for a major European carrier said in a message with a photo of the ax. Boeing's website also lists them for sale.

The crash ax has been used in the past as a weapon of last resort by pilots in crises.

In November 1985, an EgyptAir pilot said he smashed an ax into one of the Palestinian militants who hijacked his flight during a chaotic Egyptian rescue attempt in Malta that left dozens dead. In 2000, an Alaska Airlines pilot defended his cockpit with the ax when a passenger broke in and tried to crash the flight.

After Sept. 11, the crash ax became both a defensive weapon and a worry. The U.S. Air Line Pilots Association told captains to be prepared to use the ax to kill an intruder. Others worried it could be another tool for hijackers, particularly if they breached the cockpit.

"If you close the [cockpit] door and seal it up like a bank vault, that becomes a problem," U.S. Transportation Secretary Norman Mineta said at the time.

That nearly became the case on the FlyDubai flight, which had the reinforced doors common on modern aircraft that require a pilot or a combination code to enter. The flight's captain, while bleeding from the attack, said he managed a desperate lunge to open the door, allowing passengers and a backup crew access to the cockpit with just moments to spare.

Seeking Alpha analyst Louis Gerard said the deal also highlighted Constellation’s potential to play a larger role in meeting rising electricity demand from data centers.

Gerard highlighted that AES was the target of the transaction, with investors led by Global Infrastructure Partners and EQT Infrastructure VI agreeing to buy the company for $15/share in cash, at an enterprise value above $33B. PUCO’s approval for the change in control of AES Ohio was also a key regulatory step, although FERC approval is still required.

Gerard argued the rise in AES shares reflected a narrowing merger-arbitrage spread rather than a fundamental re-rating of the stock.

data.title: OpenAI safety employee quits, says 'time for trial and error is over'
data.description:
A former OpenAI safety employee who recently resigned criticized the company's approach to AI safety, arguing that a fast-paced culture focused on rapid development increases the risk of failures.

Writing in "I Quit OpenAI Because Its Culture Is Broken," published by the Atlantic on Saturday, David Robinson said AI companies, including OpenAI, were not being "nearly careful enough" and should place greater emphasis on safety expertise and research before developing more capable systems.

  • "The time for trial and error is over," Robinson wrote, arguing that advanced AI systems require safeguards more akin to those used in industries such as nuclear power and aviation.

  • Robinson said OpenAI relies heavily on what it calls "iterative deployment," releasing systems and strengthening safeguards when problems emerge.

  • The comments add to a debate within the AI industry over whether companies are moving too quickly to develop increasingly powerful systems. OpenAI and rival Anthropic have faced scrutiny after incidents in which safety controls failed, or experimental systems behaved unexpectedly.

  • Robinson, who said he spent 3-1/2 years at OpenAI, helped draft the company's preparedness framework and oversaw safety reports for 12 frontier-model launches, wrote: "As the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the level of care that I believe is needed."

  • "We're making sure our models don't become more capable than we can safely manage and secure, and we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down," an OpenAI spokesperson said in a statement.

  • Robinson also warned that AI capabilities were advancing faster than researchers' understanding of alignment, a field focused on ensuring AI systems act in accordance with human goals and values.

data.title: AbbVie, Amgen, Pfizer, GSK among participants in new 340B rebate pilot
data.description:
The Trump administration has selected 10 companies, including AbbVie , Amgen , Pfizer , and GSK , for a new pilot program that tests a rebate model for drugs purchased under a federal program that benefits uninsured and low-income patients.

Unlike the current discount model that offers savings upfront, the pilot allows the selected manufacturers to verify and pay rebates for 21 discounted drugs purchased under the government’s 340B drug pricing program.

The 340B Rebate Model Pilot takes effect on January 1 with the participation of listed drugmakers AbbVie , Amgen , Astellas , AstraZeneca , Bristol Myers , GSK , Merck , Pfizer , and Teva .

“This approach helps address compliance concerns proactively, rather than relying primarily on retrospective reviews, audits, and dispute resolution processes," said the Health Resources and Services Administration, the HHS unit overseeing the program.

The program is a flashpoint in the healthcare industry, with Big Pharma accusing some hospitals and clinics of buying 340B drugs at steep discounts but charging higher prices to pocket the difference, a charge the hospitals have vehemently denied.

The pilot marks the Trump administration’s second attempt to overhaul the decades-old drug discount program. In a setback to drugmakers, a federal judge blocked HRSA’s first 340B rebate pilot after a case brought by hospital groups last year.

data.title: Deepinder Goyal teases six Temple variants: Full list of colours, launch date, pre-order details and more
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 3 -- Deepinder Goyal's Temple wearable is getting a colourful update just as it moves closer to a wider launch.

The Zomato founder has revealed that the device will be available in six colours for its launch edition, moving beyond the single gold-coloured version that had been shown publicly earlier. The announcement comes as Temple prepares to enter its next stage, with pre-orders expected to open soon.

Goyal shared images of the six variants on 1 October, saying: "Six colors for the launch edition of @temple." He added that pre-orders would open "hopefully next week", although a couple of details still need to be finalised. People who have already joined Temple's early-access waitlist will receive priority access.

The six launch colours are True Gold, Rose Gold, Black Mirror, Real Jade, Deep Blue and Purple Funk. Until now, Temple had largely been seen in a gold finish in promotional material, making the expanded colour range one of the more visible changes ahead of its commercial rollout. It is not yet clear whether all six finishes will remain available after the launch edition.

Temple is a wearable designed to sit on the side of the head, around the temple area between the forehead and ear. Unlike conventional wearables such as smartwatches, it is intended to collect information linked to blood flow to the brain.

The technology behind it is called BrainFlow. Temple's website describes BrainFlow as a proxy for cerebral blood flow and says the device is designed to help users understand how activities such as exercise, sleep, cold exposure and meditation affect it.

The company says Temple uses optical sensing to collect signals from tissue and blood vessels around the temple. Its research programme includes studies comparing BrainFlow measurements with established research techniques, including time-domain near-infrared spectroscopy and transcranial Doppler.

Goyal has also been progressively shrinking the device. In August, he said the latest version was less than half the size of the model previously shown and described it as the smallest wearable on the market by volume. He had said at the time that a limited launch edition was expected to ship before the end of 2026.

There is currently no separate release date for each colour. The six shades are part of the launch edition itself, and Goyal's latest update indicates that pre-orders could begin as early as next week, subject to a few remaining details being confirmed. Early-access waitlist members will get priority when bookings open.

Temple's official website currently says the device will "soon" be available for pre-order and continues to invite users to join the waitlist for early access.

The final price has also not been publicly confirmed by Goyal. The Economic Times previously reported an expected price of around Rs.75,000- Rs.80,000, but that figure should not be treated as the confirmed launch price.

For now, the clearest timeline is that pre-orders are expected next week, while the limited launch edition is expected to ship before the end of 2026. The six colours - rather than just the original gold finish - are expected to form part of that launch offering.

data.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scripts history, becomes youngest Indian to win Asian Games gold at 15
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 3 -- Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became the youngest Indian to win an Asian Games gold medal on Saturday after India beat Pakistan by 19 runs in the men's cricket final at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin. Born on March 27, 2011, the Bihar opener was 15 years, six months and six days old when the gold was decided. He took the overall record from shooter Saurabh Chaudhary, who won the men's 10m air pistol title at the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta at 16 years, three months and nine days.

Captain Shreyas Iyer chose to bat. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi opened and was off in a hurry. He hit Saad Masood for two sixes before the left-arm spinner was taken out of the attack after an opening over that cost 24. On the first ball of the third over, Sooryavanshi tried a reverse sweep against Saim Ayub and was caught behind by Usman Khan for 15 off nine balls. Ayub marked the wicket with a rocking-baby celebration.

The innings did not slow. Abhishek Sharma made 61 off 28 balls, with seven sixes, and raced to a 20-ball fifty. Tilak Varma finished unbeaten on 51 off 22, and Shivam Dube added a late 27 off 15. India closed on 211/6, the highest total of the Aichi-Nagoya cricket competition.

Pakistan never quite got away. They slipped to 39/3, and Hasan Nawaz's 96 off 51 balls, with seven sixes, was left to carry the chase almost alone. He fell on the last ball. Pakistan finished on 192/6. Axar Patel and Washington Sundar each took 2 for 29, and Dube took 2 for 33.

India defended the title they won in Hangzhou in 2023. The women's side had already taken gold, so India completed a cricket double in Nagoya.

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is now the youngest Indian gold medallist at the Games, and the only 15-year-old to win one. Chaudhary still holds a separate mark. His 2018 gold was an individual title, so he remains the youngest Indian to win an individual Asian Games gold. Sooryavanshi's medal came with the men's cricket team.

Roller skater Sanjana Bathula was 15 years, three months and 11 days old when she won bronze in the women's 3000m speed skating relay at Hangzhou in 2023. Squash player Anahat Singh is next among the youngest medallists. She won bronze in the women's team event in 2023 at 15 years, six months and 16 days.

This was Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's first Asian Games. The quarterfinal against Afghanistan was washed out, so he batted only twice. In the semifinal against Sri Lanka, he made 38 off 21 balls. India then bowled Sri Lanka out for 45 and won by 124 runs. Across those two innings, he scored 53 runs at a strike rate of 176.66.

The gold sits on a list of age records that already looks crowded. He became the youngest player in IPL history at 14 years and 23 days in 2025, and the youngest centurion in men's T20 cricket at 14 years and 32 days.

data.title: Italy's Intesa raises MPS takeover offer price and warns it could drop bid
data.description:
Italy's Intesa Sanpaolo raised its takeover offer for Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS) on Saturday, saying it would pay shareholders a further €800 million ($900 million) in cash if they reject MPS's counter plan.

MPS CEO Luigi Lovaglio is seeking shareholder approval in a vote on October 29 for his strategy opposing the €34 billion share-and-cash offer Intesa announced in June - the biggest transaction so far among a dozen banking deals in Italy over the past two years.

Italian takeover rules require Lovaglio to secure shareholder backing before advancing the counter plan he unveiled in August.

Lovaglio's strategy envisages MPS making two separate all-share takeover bids for wealth manager Banca Generali and rival lender Banco BPM .

If MPS shareholders approve either of MPS' two takeover offers on October 29, that would give Intesa the right to drop its own bid based on the conditions to which the bid is subject, Intesa said.

"Intesa Sanpaolo does not intend to exercise the right to waive the conditions ... and will claim for their non-fulfilment," it said.

Meanwhile, Intesa said it would pay MPS shareholders €1.25 per share, increasing an earlier €1 euro cash component it is offering for each MPS share tendered - on top of the 1.6 newly issued Intesa shares offered for each MPS share they hold.

data.title: Bill Ackman Says He Can Size Up a CEO's Character in an Hour
data.description:
Legendary investor Bill Ackman knows the value of finding the right CEOs for companies he runs and invests in.

Picking the Right People

As the leader of Pershing Square , Ackman employs people who make financial decisions. As an activist investor, Ackman also made sure the right people were CEOs of companies he invested in.

Speaking with Shane Parrish on "The Knowledge Podcast," Ackman said he feels confident he can find the best people in the world for both roles.

"Over time, I’ve become a very good judge of people," Ackman said.

Ackman recalled helping choose Brian Niccol as CEO of Chipotle Mexican Grill when he was an investor in the restaurant company. The company picked Niccol to lead it after several food safety issues.

Niccol’s name kept coming up in conversation as a candidate, Ackman recalled. The investor said it’s important to use expert networks and talk to people who worked with a candidate and worked against or in competition with them to get a better idea about their strengths and weaknesses.

Ackman said you should look for glowing references.

In face-to-face meetings, Ackman said he can quickly get a good sense of a person’s character and honesty, which makes management decisions easier.

"You can assess that in an hour."

Read Also: Copying Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway Success Is ‘Not Sexy,’ but Bill Ackman Is Trying Anyways

Ackman on Success at 60

During the interview, Ackman reflected on his life as a man who recently turned 60. He said that being a short seller made him a villain in the past and some people have formed misconceptions of him.

Ackman said the truth is that Pershing Square has not made an activist investment since 2016 and probably won’t again.

Things have changed, and Ackman believes he has significant influence and could use dialogue and social media to push for change on any of his current or upcoming investments.

Ackman said the returns Pershing Square posts for investors are one of the main ways he measures success.

Ackman said he wants to have the greatest impact on the largest number of people, from family to friends and to the people who invested in Pershing Square, to be able to better enjoy retirement one day.

"Success for me is having a significant life."

data.title: Michael Saylor Says Strategy's STRC Is Now Steadier Than The S&P 500's Biggest Tracker: ‘A Milestone For Digital Credit’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Saylor said STRC's 30-day historical volatility has fallen to 9%, below the 10% on the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust, calling it a milestone for digital credit.
  • He described STRC and Strive's SATA as digital credit competing with private credit, high-yield bonds, and bond ETFs for income allocations.
  • The claim has narrowed since March, when his chart showed STRC at 2% and below the bond fund BND, which it now sits above.

Strategy's (MSTR) Michael Saylor said the company's Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Stretch Preferred Stock (STRC) was now less volatile than the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY), calling the move "a milestone for Digital Credit" on Saturday.

Saylor put STRC's 30-day historical volatility at 9%, against 10% for SPY. "We're harnessing the power of Bitcoin while reducing price volatility for income investors," he said.

"This is what financial engineering should do." SPY is a fund that tracks the S&P 500 (SPX) and trades like a stock.

Where STRC Ranks On Volatility

The chart measured STRC against funds that stood in for each major asset class. Strategy's own common stock was the most volatile line at 94%, with Bitcoin at 39%. SPDR Gold Shares (GLD), which tracks bullion, stood at 24%. The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq-100 index, was at 15%, and the Vanguard Real Estate ETF (VNQ) at 11%.

Only one line sat below STRC. The Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF (BND) came in at 5%, which placed Strategy's preferred between stocks and bonds on its own chart.

MSTR stock closed almost flat on Friday, down by 0.31%. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around MSTR remained in the ‘bullish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘normal’ levels over the past day.

In comparison, SPY stock closed in the green on Friday. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around SPY moved to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ while chatter around it stayed at ‘normal’ levels over the past day.

The Pitch Behind The Chart

The choice of comparisons was deliberate. Saylor set out the reasoning on Wednesday, which laid out a three-tier framework for Bitcoin treasury companies.

He described Bitcoin as digital capital, Strategy's STRC and rival Strive's (ASST) SATA as digital credit, and the two companies' common stock as digital equity. Digital credit, he wrote, competed for income allocations against private credit, high-yield bonds, preferred securities, and bond or income ETFs.

That was why STRC was being measured against SPY and BND. Saylor said that the preferred belongs in an income investor's bond sleeve, not in a crypto allocation.

He also made the case for Strive. "I want Strive to succeed," he wrote. "I want every well-managed issuer of Bitcoin-powered Digital Credit to succeed." He cited SIFMA figures putting global equity market capitalization at $157.8 trillion and global fixed-income debt at $160.7 trillion at the end of 2025, and said a tenth of one percent of either would be roughly $160 billion.

The Gap Has Narrowed

The claim Saylor made was narrower than the one he had made in March. He posted that STRC had been less volatile than every company in the S&P 500 and every major asset class over 30 days, while paying an 11.5% dividend yield. That chart cited had put STRC at 2%, below BND at 6%.

STRC now sits above BND. Volatility across the rest of the chart has fallen over the same period, with Bitcoin down from 50%, gold's tracker from 37%, QQQ from 19%, and SPY from 15%. STRC also hit a record-low volatility of 1.5% in March.

Not A Locked-In Spread

Saylor also wrote that Bitcoin appreciation was uncertain and that Bitcoin itself paid no coupon, and said the margin between long-term asset returns and financing costs has to be earned through management. "It is not a locked-in interest spread," he wrote. He added that the mechanism ran both ways, and that falling Bitcoin prices, widening credit spreads, and contracting equity multiples can reinforce one another as readily as the upside can.

data.title: FSSAI prohibits sale of 'unsafe, substandard' Nestle Low Fat Dairy Whitener, company responds
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 3 -- The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has directed an immediate ban on sale of Nestle India's "low-fat dairy whitener". The food regulator called the product "unsafe and substandard" on Saturday.

A sample of "low-fat dairy whitener" manufactured by Nestle India has failed the safety test conducted by FSSAI. FSSAI said that the sample, which was collected from the premises of Hotel Lalit in Connaught Place, New Delhi, has been found "unsafe and substandard".

Nestle denied the allegations and said, "Nestle Low Fat Dairy Whitener is safe to consume and complies with all applicable regulatory requirements. Phosphorus is a nutrient that occurs naturally in milk and is therefore present in all milk-based products."

"FSSAI lab reports reflect total phosphorus against the additive limit, without accounting for the substantial natural phosphorus contribution from milk-based ingredients. Our product is in full compliance for added phosphorus as per prescribed limits under FSSR including for as consumed basis. We have been in continuous engagement with the authorities as per due process established under law and have shared data across other same/similar milk-based products in the category to reflect presence of naturally occurring phosphorous." the statement from Nestle read.

Via a post on X, FSSAI said that the product was found "substandard" and "unsafe" as per the report of the food analyst's laboratory, violating the Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act, 2006.

The regulator added that a copy of the laboratory analysis report was provided to the food business operator (FBO) for reference and necessary action.

A notice has been sent to Bharat Hotels Ltd over the product and its non-compliance.

Under the relevant section of the FSS Act, 2006, the FBO was eligible to appeal against the food analyst's report within a prescribed time period.

FSSAI has now directed the FBO to immediately stop the sale of the identified food product.

"A sample of Nestle "Low Fat Dairy Whitener" collected from M/s Bharat Hotels Ltd. (The Lalit), New Delhi, has been declared UNSAFE & SUBSTANDARD by Food Analyst reports under the FSS Act 2006," read the post on social media.

Previously, FSSAI had flagged Nestle India's infant nutrition products. The food regulator initiated legal action against Nestle India Ltd in three cases over alleged promotional violations and nutritional non-compliance in its infant food portfolio.

The legal proceedings involved promotional claims for two infant formula brands, NAN Excella Pro Stage 1 and Lactogen Pro 1, as well as a follow-up formula sample that didn't meet prescribed nutritional parameters in laboratory tests.

"In NAN Excella Pro Stage 1, claims relating to '5 HMOs' and 'Whey Protein' were observed, while in Lactogen Pro 1, a claim relating to 'Whey Protein' being easy to digest was observed. Accordingly, clarifications were sought from M/s Nestle India Limited regarding the above claims," FSSAI said.

"Both products were found to be in contravention of Regulation 4(2) of the FSS (Foods for Infant Nutrition) Regulations, 2020, which restricts promotional claims/material intended to increase the saleability of infant foods, and Section 3 of the IMS Act, 1992, which prohibits their advertisement and promotion," FSSAI added.

However, Nestle India had maintained that it remains compliant with all applicable regulations in India.

data.title: Review of Sony BRAVIA Theatre Bar 7, Sub 8, Rear 8
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 3 -- I want to start by saying that you can actually enjoy movies best at the cinema, but you cannot easily replicate that experience or have it when it comes to shows/series at home. This is where having a good sound system adds a lot of stuff. It completely redefines the viewing experience. Entertainment cannot be just visuals only.

Sound adds the real depth, the feel, the essence, and without it, you are only receiving half the artistic intent of a scene.

To truly understand the value of what sound is all about, I want you to look beyond the basic acoustic limitations of modern televisions.

Today's displays are remarkably thin, which leaves absolutely no physical cabinet space for speaker drivers to move air. The result is a flat, lifeless acoustic signature. I have been testing a modular trio from Sony for quite some time, claiming to solve this problem.

This trio system consists of the BRAVIA Theatre Bar 7 (Rs 99,990) handling the front and height channels, the BRAVIA Theatre Sub 8 (Rs 42,990) delivering the low-frequency rumble, and the BRAVIA Theatre Rear 8 wireless speakers (Rs 42,990) wrapping the room in immersive surround sound. Let me tell you all about my experience when I combined them to find out if this trio system is the best home theater setup that you can have.

BRAVIA Theatre Bar 7:

The centerpiece of this entire system is the BRAVIA Theatre Bar 7. Visually, it is a sleek, low-profile soundbar wrapped in an acoustic fabric that slips seamlessly under your television. But inside the chassis, it is an engineered powerhouse. The Bar 7 packs nine dedicated speaker units, including side-firing drivers and up-firing units designed to physically bounce height channels off your ceiling.

From an audiophile standpoint, what the Bar 7 does flawlessly is anchor the vocal clarity. Credit to its dedicated center channel processing, dialogues are crisp and well-separated from the chaotic background noise of an action sequence. It supports the heavy-hitting spatial formats like Dolby Atmos and DTS:X, and is even IMAX Enhanced.

However, if there is one caveat to the Bar 7 as a standalone unit, it is the lower frequency response. It delivers crystal-clear mids and highs, but because of its compact volume, it simply does not get low or loud enough on its own to provide a truly cinematic punch. I guess that's exactly why it requires the rest of the trio.

BRAVIA Theatre Sub 8:

This is where the BRAVIA Theatre Sub 8 comes into play, and it completely transforms the acoustic signature of the system. A soundbar handles the intricate directional details, but a dedicated subwoofer is what gives the audio its physical weight and presence.

Armed with a 300W amplifier and a large 200mm driver unit, the Sub 8 handles the heavy lifting for the low-end frequencies. In the audio world, a good sub doesn't just make noise; it moves air.

You stop just hearing an explosion on screen and start actually feeling the shockwave reverberate through the floorboards. What impressed me the most is how well the crossover is managed. The Sub 8 delivers propulsive, controlled bass that grounds the action sequences without ever muddying the mid-range or overpowering the vocals coming from the Bar 7.

BRAVIA Theatre Rear 8:

As pristine as the front stage and bass are, the system achieves true immersiveness when you add the BRAVIA Theatre Rear 8 wireless speakers. These two speakers add the 5.1 kind of depth that you absolutely need. When you install them and set them up behind the backside of where you sit, that placement makes things profoundly immersive.

It is here that Sony's 360 'Spatial Sound Mapping' goes into overdrive. The system does not just passively push sound to the back of the room; it mathematically generates multiple 'phantom speakers' in a dome around and above you.

When a helicopter flies past on the screen, you genuinely hear the rotors move seamlessly from the front Bar 7, across the ceiling, and fade into the Rear 8s behind you. All of a sudden, I started to feel as if I am genuinely watching a movie in a premium commercial theater. They elevate the soundstage from a flat, two-dimensional plane to a living, breathing environment.

The Setup Experience:

This Sony trio is easily the easiest setup I have ever experienced. You simply place the units in their respective spots, plug them into a power outlet, and open the smartphone app.

The BRAVIA Connect app takes care of everything. There is no complicated calibration microphone to wave around the room. The system uses 'Sound Field Optimization', sending out a quick pulse of sound to digitally map your specific room's acoustic characteristics. Within seconds, it calibrates the sound field height and optimizes the spatial mapping for your exact seating position. And if you are an enthusiast who wants to tinker, the app allows for pro-level customizations, letting you adjust the sound field, voice modes, and individual rear speaker levels to perfectly match your preferences.

Non-5.1 Content:

At times, if the content is not natively 5.1 or Dolby Atmos ready, the system can struggle slightly with the upmixing. When you are watching standard stereo broadcasts or compressed streaming video, the audio can become very heavy when the sound goes up. Because Sony's upmixing algorithm is aggressive in trying to utilize all the physical and phantom speakers, standard flat audio is pushed hard into the surround channels.

This can make the background score or ambient noise feel dense and overwhelming in the lower frequencies. Thankfully, it is quite normal when the vocals are active; dialogue never gets lost. But the balance you hear on a 4K Blu-ray can occasionally feel a bit artificially inflated on basic content.

In The End:

If you are planning to invest in this setup, here is my practical take on getting the best out of it. First, running the Sound Field Optimization in the BRAVIA Connect app is non-negotiable; skipping it leaves the spatial audio flat, whereas running it properly maps the phantom speakers to your ceiling height and room dimensions.

Second, definitely make use of the app's 'Voice Mode' for poorly mixed movies where action effects tend to drown out dialogues, it isolates speech cleanly without distorting the rest of the mix. I think, buying the Bar 7 without the Sub 8 is an incomplete experience, so go for the trio to bring in a sense of authority that true home cinema demands.

For a few of you, I do not expect this trio to double as a dedicated audiophile Hi-Fi setup for stereo music streaming. And the reason is simple. In my opinion, this trio is tuned specifically for cinematic theatricality, where standard music tracks can occasionally feel a bit clinical or bass-heavy. If you're an enthusiast then do note that there are no manual multiband EQ controls (you rely on Sony's automated Sound Field profiles).

Then there is no alphanumeric LED display on the front grille, so you have to glance at the TV or phone app just to check volume levels and active codecs. Last but not least, there are occasional momentary audio dropouts over HDMI during dead-silent scenes where the bar momentarily sleeps and clips the very first syllable when audio resumes.

Despite that minor quirk with standard audio, Sony has proved their mettle in terms of what they have done with this ecosystem. The combination of the Bar 7, Sub 8, and Rear 8 delivers an expansive, surreal soundstage that redefines home entertainment. So yes, it is simply one of the best.

My Rating: 4/5

data.title: 5 public sector banks post 15-25% credit growth in Q2FY27
data.description:
Public sector banks (PSBs) seem to have done fairly well on credit growth in the second quarter (Q2) of FY27, posting year-on-year (yoy) growth in the 15-25 per cent range, even as the gap between credit growth and deposit growth persists.

Deposit growth has ranged from 7 per cent to 14 per cent yoy, lagging credit growth, according to provisional business figures disclosed by five PSBs so far.

As per RBI’s latest data (August) on sectoral deployment of bank credit, the demand has been higher vis-a-vis the year-ago period across all four segments -- agriculture and allied activities, industry, services and personal loans.

PNB’s advances grow 14.8 per cent

Punjab National Bank (PNB) reported a 14.8 per cent yoy growth in gross advances and 9.9 per cent growth in total deposits. As at September-end 2026, the bank’s gross advances and total deposits stood at ₹13,42,693 crore and ₹17,77,097 crore, respectively.

Within gross advances and total deposits, PNB’s domestic advances and domestic deposits were up 12.59 per cent yoy (to stand at ₹12,58,583 crore as at September-end 2026) and 9.44 per cent yoy (to ₹17,11,696 crore), respectively.

As at September-end 2026, the gap between domestic credit and advances growth stood at 315 basis points. One basis point equals one-hundredth of a percentage point.

Union Bank sees 18.53 per cent growth

Union Bank of India (UBI) clocked an 18.53 per cent yoy growth in gross advances and 6.87 per cent growth in total deposits. As at September-end 2026, the bank’s gross advances and total deposits stood at ₹11,55,930 crore and ₹13,19,457 crore, respectively.

Within gross advances and total deposits, UBI’s domestic advances and domestic deposits were up 17.36 per cent yoy (to stand at ₹11,05,807 crore as at September-end 2026) and 6.88 per cent yoy (to ₹13,18,977 crore), respectively. As at September-end 2026, the gap between domestic credit and advances growth stood at 1,048 basis points.

The share of RAM (Retail, Agriculture and Micro, Small & Medium Enterprise) advances in UBI’s domestic advances declined to 57.47 per cent as at September-end 2026, from 58.82 per cent as at September-end 2025.

The proportion of CASA (Current Account, Savings Account) deposits in UBI’s domestic deposits improved to 34.93 per cent as at September-end 2026, up from 32.56 per cent as at September-end 2025.

Indian Bank reports 16.6 per cent growth

Indian Bank reported a 16.6 per cent yoy growth in gross advances and 12.4 per cent growth in total deposits. As at September-end 2026, the bank’s gross advances and total deposits stood at ₹7.23 lakh crore and ₹8.73 lakh crore, respectively.

The share of CASA deposits in Indian Bank’s domestic deposits improved to 39.28 per cent as at September-end 2026, up from 38.87 per cent as at September-end 2025.

UCO Bank, P&SB post double-digit growth

UCO Bank recorded a 24.68 per cent yoy growth in gross advances and 14.05 per cent growth in total deposits. As at September-end 2026, the bank’s gross advances and total deposits stood at ₹2.88 lakh crore and ₹3.49 lakh crore, respectively.

Punjab & Sind Bank reported a 19.37 per cent yoy growth in gross advances and 12.98 per cent growth in total deposits. As at September-end 2026, the bank’s gross advances and total deposits stood at ₹1,26,011 crore and ₹1,53,317 crore, respectively.

data.title: Tennessee prison chief resigns after failed execution
data.description:
By Sheila Dang

The head of the Tennessee Department of Correction will step down this month, state officials said on Saturday, days after convicted murderer Christa Pike was left gravely ill from the state's failed attempt to execute her by lethal injection.

The botched execution on Wednesday left Pike unconscious, intubated and hooked to a mechanical ventilator to breathe, her lawyers wrote in a Friday court filing. It is the state's second failed execution attempt this year, prompting Tennessee Governor Bill Lee to halt attempts to carry out the death penalty for the rest of 2026.

Lee said on Saturday that Frank Strada has resigned as Department of Correction commissioner and would leave his position this month. The governor had ordered an independent review of the execution attempt at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville, the state capital.

Strada, in a separate statement, said that although he believes his agency's personnel followed proper protocol, "stepping aside is in the best interest of Tennesseans as the independent review moves forward."

An interim commissioner will be announced later, the governor's office said.

"Commissioner Strada has served with integrity, and I appreciate his willingness to put the interests of Tennesseans first during this difficult moment,” Lee said in a statement.

Pike's lawyers have accused Correction Department officials of ignoring prior warnings from her doctors that her small veins and a blood disorder called thrombocytosis would make placing intravenous lines especially difficult.

Pike, 50, was convicted three decades ago of first-degree murder for her role in the torture and killing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in 1995, when Pike was 18.

Doctors were working to save Pike's life and clear the drug pentobarbital from her system, her lawyers said on Friday.

data.title: BlackRock's IBIT ETF Flashes Golden Cross As SEC Approves Triple-Leveraged Bitcoin, Ethereum ETPs
data.description:
Key points:
  • BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF has its 50-day average moving above its 200-day average.
  • The SEC approved a Cboe BZX rule change on Friday to allow listing of six 3x leveraged products from Volatility Shares’ VS Trust.
  • Trading in each fund can only begin once the fund's registration has become effective.

BlackRock’s (BLK) iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) flashed a golden cross on Saturday, as the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved a rule change to allow triple-leveraged Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH) products to be listed.

According to Koyfin data, IBIT’s 50-day simple moving average (SMA) was 41.97, only up from its 200-day average of 41.92. The shorter average crosses above the longer one to form a golden cross. Traders often read it as a bullish sign.

SoSoValue data showed US spot Bitcoin (BTC) exchange-traded funds began October with new inflows. The funds had net inflows of $102.67 million on Oct. 1. Topping the list was BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF with $195.57 million.

IBIT’s inflow exceeded the group’s net inflow. SoSoValue data showed total net assets across the funds hit $109.34 billion. Net inflows through October 1 for the week to date were $51.25 million

Leveraged Bitcoin, Ethereum Funds Approved

In addition to the daily flows, the SEC implemented an action that could broaden the selection of Bitcoin products.

The SEC approved a Cboe BZX Exchange rule change on Friday, according to a filing. It allows six of the products from Volatility Shares’ VS Trust to list on the exchange. Each seeks three times the daily return of its benchmark. The lineup includes Bitcoin and Ethereum (ETH) as well as gold, silver, crude oil and natural gas.

Volatility Shares has previously filed for leveraged crypto funds. In its 2023 filing for the 2x Bitcoin Strategy ETF (BITX), the firm said such funds seek to achieve a set multiple of daily returns. It also pointed out that returns over longer periods can diverge from that multiple and can even move in the reverse direction. The new products put leveraged crypto alongside commodity funds.

No trading in any fund shall occur before the fund's registration becomes effective, and no trading date will be set.

Bitcoin’s price was trading around $84,800, down over 0.2% in the last 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC dropped to ‘bearish’ from the ‘neutral’ zone, as chatter rose to ‘normal’ from ‘low’ levels over the past day.

data.title: "Unique programme": CM Naidu highlights IIT alumni network at PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit 2026
data.description:
Vijayawada, Oct. 3 -- Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Saturday described the PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit 2026 as a unique initiative and highlighted the potential of leveraging the knowledge and expertise of IIT alumni to help develop the state into a global knowledge hub.

Speaking to ANI, Naidu said, "This is a unique program. India has 5 lakh IIT alumni. If you see these alumni, if you use that knowledge, we can do wonders. That is why, for the first time, they are establishing the World Amaravati IITians Council. They are going to give ideas continuously, subject-wise. They are going to involve universities, all IITs, to work together. This is where knowledge will be exchanged, and we will prepare for tomorrow. Ultimately, Andhra Pradesh is going to benefit by becoming a global knowledge hub."

The maiden PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit 2026, organised by PanIIT Alumni India in collaboration with the Government of Andhra Pradesh, brought together IIT leaders, policymakers, industry leaders, entrepreneurs, investors, academicians, technology experts and innovators to discuss a long-term technology and innovation roadmap for Andhra Pradesh.

According to an official release, the summit was formally inaugurated by Nara Lokesh, Minister for Information Technology, Electronics & Communications, Government of Andhra Pradesh, with the ceremonial lighting of the lamp by Katamneni, IAS, Secretary, Department of ITE&C, Government of Andhra Pradesh; KN Satyanarayana, Director, IIT Tirupati; V Kamakoti, Director, IIT Madras; Anand Kumar, MD, STMicroelectronics India; and Mall.

He was joined by Swadeep Pillarisetti, Chair, PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit 2026; Amitabh Ranjan, Vice Chairman, PanIIT Alumni India; Prabhat Kumar, IRS, Chairman, PanIIT Alumni India; Bhaskar Katamneni, IAS, Secretary, Department of ITE&C, Government of Andhra Pradesh; KN Satyanarayana, Director, IIT Tirupati; V Kamakoti, Director, IIT Madras; Anand Kumar, MD, STMicroelectronics India; and Mallik Tatipamula, CTO, Ericsson Silicon Valley.

Held at Dr BR Ambedkar Kala Vedika, Vijayawada, the Summit was themed "Andhra's Resilient DeepTech Decade: Anchored by PanIIT- Swarna Andhra to Viksit Bharat 2047." The Summit sought to connect the collective strength of the 23 IITs and the global 5-lakh-plus IIT alumni network with Andhra Pradesh's development priorities.

The day-long Summit featured intensive discussions on some of the most critical technology and development priorities.

The sessions covered Energy in the Age of AI; DeepTech in All Walks of Life and Product Perfection; Space, Aerospace & Defence Manufacturing; Bio Valley- Health Access & Screening at Scale; and AgriTech- Farmers & Water Security.

The discussions brought together senior representatives from government, IITs, global technology companies, industry and startups, including experts from IBM, NXP Semiconductors, Ericsson, AWS, Honeywell Aerospace, Apollo Hospitals, ICMR, ICRISAT and leading Indian technology and manufacturing companies.

The Summit also featured fireside conversations on Skilling & Entrepreneurship and AI in Governance, besides a presentation on Amaravati Capital City.

The Valedictory Session presented a series of institutional initiatives designed to create sustained engagement between PanIIT, the IIT ecosystem, the Andhra Pradesh Government and industry.

PanIIT Amaravati Council, a proposed permanent platform and secretariat in Amaravati to connect the global IIT alumni network with Andhra Pradesh's long-term development agenda.

PanIIT Amaravati Venture Fund, a DeepTech investment mechanism aimed at supporting entrepreneurship and high-potential ventures in the State.

Global IIT Mentor Network, a proposed 100-member network to connect entrepreneurs, startups and young talent in Andhra Pradesh with experienced IIT alumni globally.

Industry Chairs, 10 proposed industry-linked chairs to strengthen research and industry-academia collaboration.

IIT Technology Transfer Pipeline, an initiative to identify and facilitate the commercialisation of technologies emerging from IITs.

DeepTech Policy Package, a proposed policy framework covering areas including AI, quantum technologies, semiconductors, energy, space, defence, healthcare, AgriTech and skilling.

The official Summit framework also identifies these initiatives as part of a longer-term PanIIT-Andhra Pradesh engagement.

One of the key moments of the Summit was the launch of Q-Shiva, involving five quantum computers, positioning quantum technology among the frontier areas being explored for Andhra Pradesh's emerging DeepTech ecosystem.

The programme also featured a demonstration by the Qubit Force team and the launch of the book "Quantum Children."

The Summit's discussions extended across Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, DeepTech, Quantum Computing, Semiconductors and Data Centres, MedTech and Healthcare, Oil & Gas and Green Energy, Space and Aerospace, Defence and AgriTech.

Three strategic roundtables were conducted in parallel, bringing together IIT Directors, venture capitalists and family offices, and industry leaders and unicorn CXOs. The roundtables focused on converting the Summit's ideas into partnerships, investments and institutional initiatives.

The Summit also included a technology exhibition and networking sessions connecting startups, investors, industry and the IIT ecosystem. It has about 50 stalls.

Prabhat Kumar, IRS, Chairman, PanIIT Alumni India, said that the Summit represents an opportunity to channel the collective strength of IIT alumni towards institution-building, innovation and nation-building.

Amitabh Ranjan, Vice Chairman, PanIIT Alumni India, said the objective was to create institutions and networks that would continue to work beyond the Summit, including a Council, venture fund, fellowship and mentor network.

Swadeep Pillarisetti, Chair, PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit 2026, and Shri Sudhakar Gande, Chair/leadership representatives associated with the Summit, were among those who contributed to the initiative.

PanIIT Alumni India is the umbrella organisation representing alumni of all 23 Indian Institutes of Technology, with a global community of more than 500,000 alumni. Its objective is to channel the collective expertise, networks and resources of the IIT alumni community towards innovation, entrepreneurship, technology transfer and nation-building.

The PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit 2026 concluded with the presentation of the PanIIT Amaravati initiatives, the Andhra PanIIT Declaration, the Q-Shiva launch and a roadmap for continued collaboration.

The Summit is positioned as the beginning of a longer-term engagement linking IIT talent, research, technology, entrepreneurship, capital and industry with Andhra Pradesh's development priorities.

The objective is clear: to build partnerships that move DeepTech from ideas and laboratories to products, enterprises and solutions contributing to Andhra Pradesh's journey towards Swarna Andhra 2047 and India's Viksit Bharat 2047.

data.title: ShinyHunters hacker in FBI data theft detained in Jordan, cooperating with bureau, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • Khader was detained by Jordanian authorities this week, three sources say
  • Two sources say Khader is cooperating with FBI to identify fellow ShinyHunters hackers
  • Reuters analysis finds stolen data includes FBI employees' medical, psychiatric and personal information

By Jana Winter, Raphael Satter and AJ Vicens

A suspected member of the ShinyHunters hacking group, which says it stole data on every FBI employee, was detained in Jordan this week and is cooperating with the FBI, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

Saif al-Din Khader was detained by Jordanian authorities, the three sources said. Two of them said he was brought into custody on Tuesday. Reuters could not immediately determine the circumstances of Khader’s detention or where he is being held. Two sources said that he is helping the FBI and global law enforcement locate the other hackers in the group.

The FBI declined to comment on any specific arrest or activity abroad but said that the bureau "continues to aggressively investigate the recent cyber incident allegedly involving ShinyHunters, having already worked with partners to arrest multiple subjects — and we will spare no resource in bringing each of the responsible individuals to justice."

Reuters’ attempts to reach Khader and members of his family over the past week and a half have been unsuccessful.

The detention of Khader — whose alleged hacker nickname is Rey — is the latest twist in the case of ShinyHunters. The prolific cyber extortion group, which has a long history of targeting major corporations around the world, is believed by experts to consist mainly of young, English-speaking hackers focused on data theft and extortion.

Their theft of what they claim are mountains of data on every single FBI employee has drawn comparisons to the allegedly Chinese-linked intrusion at the US Office of Personnel Management in 2015, which compromised sensitive details on millions of Americans who had been vetted for security clearances.

SENSITIVE INFORMATION

A Reuters analysis of a sample of the data shared by ShinyHunters revealed that the data contained extensive personally identifiable information of FBI employees, sensitive job role information, and psychiatric and medical information.

Khader's cooperation with investigators could be critical to helping contain — or at least understand — the damage. One source said he was walking investigators through his electronic devices and digital correspondence to help the FBI locate his cohorts.

"His cooperation is critical to ongoing efforts to arrest these hackers," the source told Reuters.

There have been hints for days that ShinyHunters was experiencing disruption following the announcement of its break-in at the FBI. Beginning on Tuesday, Reuters was unable to reach ShinyHunters through the online account it previously used to communicate with journalists. Then, on Wednesday, the group’s dark web site, where it had previously posted threats to the FBI, disappeared.

FBI Director Kash Patel had been hinting at more arrests following the announcement that another alleged ShinyHunters member, Pepijn van der Stap, had been detained in the Netherlands.

“FBI teams are working new leads RIGHT NOW,” Patel said on Wednesday in a message posted to X. “More arrests are on the table.”

The operators of a ShinyHunters-linked email address did not respond to a request for comment on Friday. The operators of that email account previously told Reuters that the group’s site had gone offline due to sabotage from rivals and "disruption due to an unrelated incident."

The group had previously struck a defiant note, saying on September 22 that it had hacked the FBI in retaliation over an advisory that accused ShinyHunters of making "exaggerated claims of access" to extort victims for money. It gave the FBI a week to withdraw the advisory.

But in the most recent email to Reuters, the operators struck a conciliatory tone, saying that “we want no further escalation” with the FBI. The operators said Reuters could interpret their message as meaning, “ShinyHunters backing down completely.”

KHADER'S IDENTITY LONG KNOWN

Khader’s identity, and his alleged connection to ShinyHunters, have long been known to security researchers.

Last year, the independent journalist Brian Krebs reported that Khader was a key member of Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters, an umbrella group of hackers that included ShinyHunters. Krebs, who said he spoke to Khader over Signal, quoted the teenager as saying he had quit the world of data breaches and extortion and was cooperating with law enforcement.

But ShinyHunters continued its hacking spree into 2026, claiming credit for break-ins at video game developer Rockstar Games, the maker of "Grand Theft Auto," and a May intrusion involving education tool Canvas that ⁠caused widespread ​disruption across US schools.

Law enforcement agencies around the world, including in the United States, have struggled to arrest and prosecute members of related groups such as Lapsus$ or Scattered Spider, Reuters has previously reported.

Sources told Reuters that the difficulty stems from the hackers’ young ages, which can make prosecutions complex, or because the groups they belong to are so chaotic and informal, or because victims of their extortion attempts often decline to help investigators.

data.title: Trump offering $90 to Medicare enrollees to cover premiums
data.description:
The Trump administration will soon start paying $90 each to more than 20M Medicare enrollees to help them pay for their Part B premiums, marking the latest financial incentive offered by the White House ahead of the midterm elections.

The one-time payments are expected to reach eligible Medicare enrollees in the form of a direct deposit or a check in early October, according to a White House fact sheet on Friday.

However, of the roughly 64M participants in the government-backed healthcare program, some enrollees, including recipients of Medicaid for premium payments, will not be eligible for the one-time payments.

The funds will be utilized from the Medicare Improvement Fund, which Congress established in 2008 with $2.2B to improve the Medicare fee-for-service program.

In a social media post announcing the payments, Trump identified the fund as “a pointless 'Slush Fund'" that Democrats created to "pay for the Waste, Fraud, and Abuse for their Special Interest friends, and drive up Healthcare costs.”

Medicare Part B covers doctor visits, treatments administered in doctors' offices, and preventative tests. The payments will be separate from the $500 checks the administration began sending to nearly 1M Americans enrolled in Affordable Care Act plans last Thursday, Trump said.

Leading health insurers: UnitedHealth , Humana , Cigna , CVS Health , Clover Health , Alignment Healthcare , Oscar Health , Centene , Molina Health , and Elevance Health .

data.description:
Here’s a challenge. Using the five clues below, identify the company that is being talked about here.

1 I have undergone several mergers and changes in control over my history of less than five decades.

2 My chairman is a member of several illustrious boards and is well respected for successful joint ventures, as well as a few hostile ones.

3 One of my founding promoters made a complete exit through an IPO recently.

4 My valuation quadrupled within three years of listing, but lost half its value over the subsequent year.

5 I am a small-cap stock despite belonging to a multi-billion-dollar group and being an industry leader in a sub-segment of a large industry.
